22193db121333fea: KUALA LUMPUR: The atmosphere behind Block B of 1Razak Mansion in Salak South was lively on Wednesday morning.

The laughter of elderly residents from various ethnic backgrounds could be heard from afar as they gathered at the open space to tend to vegetables, fruits and herbs they have been growing for the past eight months.

The site, aptly named the 'Food Forest', has become more than just a place to grow fresh produce. It has evolved into a space where neighbours come together, exercise, share gardening skills and enjoy the fruits of their labour.

"Look over there. I planted that area three months ago, and the chillies have already started growing. There are quite a lot of them," said 75-year-old Siti Hanah Ahmad, pointing to a small plot at one corner of the site.
Another resident, Azni Saharin, 67, said she was delighted to see the fruits of their efforts.

"It is wonderful to see what we have grown. Not only does it help us save on household expenses, but we also get to share our gardening and cooking skills," she said, pointing to a misai kucing plant with the aid of her walking stick.
For 64-year-old Alice Fernandez, the Food Forest is also a place to relax and connect with her neighbours.
"It's a good way to connect with nature and relax the mind. Without this space, residents would just be stuck at home with not much to do, which is not good for their mental well-being.

"In fact, we also have the opportunity to cook and enjoy nasi ulam together, which was introduced by our Malay neighbours. We enjoyed the process of making it and were amazed that we could come together to appreciate our traditional food," she said.
BRINGING AN ABANDONED SPACE TO LIFE
It is hard to imagine that the 560-square-foot Food Forest was once an abandoned site overgrown with weeds and bushes.
Today, it has become a favourite spot for residents to relax, socialise and share their harvests.

1Razak Mansion Management Corporation (MC) chairman Anthony Tan said residents previously avoided the area as it was located near a hall often used for funeral ceremonies and a rubbish room that sometimes emitted unpleasant odours.

"However, since the beginning of this year, in January, after the site was cleaned up and transformed into a Food Forest, it has become a source of pride for the residents of 1Razak Mansion and our favourite place to spend time outdoors," he told Bernama.
He said the project had so far introduced more than 80 species of plants, vegetables and herbs, involving 60 residents.

"Besides greening the area around 1Razak Mansion, we are also working to reduce solid waste through recycling and composting, while preserving and rehabilitating the area around Sungai Kerayong, which is located next to our residential blocks," he said.

The initiative, spearheaded by PWD Smart FarmAbility Sdn Bhd founder and social entrepreneur Dr Billy Tang Chee Seng, 60, together with residents, is intended to go beyond conventional urban farming by combining food security, environmental rehabilitation, healthy ageing and community participation.
MORE THAN FOOD: SUPPORTING HEALTHY AGEING

In an urban environment where space is limited and ageing residents can easily become disconnected from community activities, Tang believes food production can help reconnect people with their neighbours, nature and a sense of purpose.
For him, the Food Forest is part of a broader Soil-U-tion Regenerative Ecosystem, which explores how food production, soil health and community participation can contribute to healthy ageing.

"It (the Food Forest) is more than an urban farming project. We aim to create a self-sustaining ecosystem where residents, especially elderly and low-income households, can grow nutritious food, learn about soil health, participate in environmental restoration and eventually develop skills that can generate income or improve their quality of life," he said.
He said weekly activities including Tai Chi, Zumba, cooking classes and Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) services were also held for residents.
"Now even our Chinese residents enjoy eating nasi ulam made from what they have planted.
"This also creates a harmonious community, where the Food Forest can serve as a place for exchanging cultures and learning from each other," he said.
FROM FOOD FOREST 1.0 TO 2.0

Tang said the Food Forest at 1Razak Mansion represents Food Forest 1.0, a community-based model that combines food growing with participation by older residents, shared harvests, environmental stewardship, experiential learning and social regeneration.

He said both Food Forest 1.0 and the proposed Food Forest 2.0 form part of a broader Community Regeneration Infrastructure (CRI) approach, in which food production is used as an entry point to strengthen food security, community participation, environmental awareness and healthier living.
The next phase is envisioned at Lot 601 in Batang Kali, where Food Forest 2.0 is being developed as a healthy-ageing "living laboratory" and ESG-SDG Learning Centre.

The concept is intended to expand the model through regenerative food forests, biodiversity restoration, soil regeneration, experiential learning, intergenerational participation and a Food as Medicine pathway focused on nutrition, preventive-health awareness and healthier lifestyles.
It is also expected to explore opportunities associated with the silver economy, including ways for older people to continue contributing their knowledge, experience and skills.

Rather than viewing senior citizens solely as recipients of care, Tang said the model seeks to create enabling environments in which they can remain active participants, growers, learners, mentors and community stewards.
Food Forest 1.0 therefore provides a community-scale demonstration of the approach, while Food Forest 2.0 is intended to deepen its learning, measurement, research and replication potential.
A REGENERATIVE FOOD SYSTEM

Rather than functioning solely as a conventional community garden focused on planting and harvesting vegetables, Tang said the Food Forest concept was designed around a broader regenerative ecosystem that links food production with soil restoration, biodiversity, nutrition education, circular resource use and community participation.
"I don't do farming. Farming is very difficult. I innovate tools to connect people, nature and the planet. That's what I do," he said.

This philosophy also underpins the Soil-U-tion Regenerative Aquaponics Satellite Farm, one of the tools developed to bring food production and environmental learning into space-constrained settings such as residential communities, schools, elderly homes and welfare centres.
The aquaponics component creates a recirculating relationship between fish and plants.

Tang explained that tilapia raised in tanks naturally produce waste containing nutrients. Beneficial microorganisms within the system help convert nitrogen compounds into forms that can be taken up by plants.
"As the plants absorb these nutrients, they also help improve the quality of the circulating water before it returns to the fish tank, creating a natural nutrient cycle," he said.
The approach can be combined with soil-based growing systems, enabling communities to use both soil and soilless cultivation within an integrated food-production environment.

Tang said the objective was not merely to install agricultural equipment, but to create accessible tools through which communities could learn about food, water, soil, biodiversity, waste reduction and resource efficiency through practical experience.
FROM LIVING SOIL TO HEALTHY COMMUNITIES
Tang said the Soil-U-tion concept extends beyond the production and consumption of fresh food.
Its broader Food as Medicine pathway explores the relationship between healthy soil, nutritious food, dietary diversity, fermentation, gut-health literacy and community well-being.
The concept describes this progression as:
"Living Soil → Living Food → Living Gut → Living Minds → Living Communities."
Tang said controlled fermentation and fermented foods could form part of future learning and research activities examining how food production, nutrition and microbial processes interact.

The concept does not position food or fermented products as substitutes for medical treatment. Instead, it seeks to connect regenerative agriculture with nutrition education, preventive-health awareness, healthy ageing and community well-being.
"The bigger vision is to help people understand that soil, food, health, education and community are not separate issues. They are interconnected," Tang said.
Another tool introduced to residents is the Eco-HOPE Box, a compact household growing system designed for people with little or no previous farming experience.

Residents are taught basic soil stewardship, moisture management and simple pH monitoring, as well as harvesting methods that allow suitable vegetables to continue regenerating instead of removing the entire plant after a single harvest.

Household resources such as rice-washing water may also be reused where appropriate as part of the growing process, helping participants understand practical links between food production, water use, resource recovery and waste reduction.

Tang said these activities form part of the wider ESG-SDG Learning Centre approach, where sustainability is learned not only through theory but through everyday actions that can be observed, practised and, where possible, measured.

Under the Community Regeneration Infrastructure model, he said the aim was ultimately to move communities from recipients to stewards, from food insecurity towards greater food resilience, and from sustainability awareness towards practical action.
RESTORING BIODIVERSITY
Beyond food production, Tang said the team had observed changes in the immediate environment since the Food Forest was established.
He said bees began appearing around the project within four months, while birds and earthworms were also observed returning to the area.
"The residents here were very excited to see the Food Forest surrounded by bees and butterflies.
"It has demonstrated that biodiversity can coexist even within densely developed urban communities if suitable conditions are created," he said.

Tang said the Food Forest was also being developed as an educational space and learning centre, particularly for corporations seeking to practise Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) principles.
University students have also been brought into his wider network of community projects for internships involving human nutrition and sustainability.

"Rather than placing students within a single discipline or organisation, I want them to experience an 'internship ecosystem', where food, health, the environment and community development intersect," he said.

"At 1Razak Mansion, the residents themselves are part of that learning process. They are taught how to assess soil conditions, maintain plants and understand the principles behind the system, rather than simply being given equipment and told what to grow."

For Tang, the objective of the Food Forest is not necessarily to make the community completely self-sufficient in food, but to build enough knowledge, skills and community capacity for residents to respond when food affordability or supply becomes a challenge.
"At least if anything happens, they can grow food for their community," he said.
– BERNAMA

e794a5654734b4e4: KUALA LUMPUR: Butterfield FB Bhd got off to a bitter start on its ACE Market debut today, opening at 43 sen, five sen or 10.42 per cent below its initial public offering (IPO) price of 48 sen.
The coffee and tea extract powder maker slipped further to 41.5 sen, down 6.5 sen or 13.54 per cent from its IPO price, before clawing back some of the losses.
At 9.18am, Butterfield FB was trading at 44.5 sen, down 3.5 sen or 7.29 per cent, with 24.23 million shares changing hands. It was the third most actively traded stock on the exchange.
The weak debut came after the company's IPO drew strong investor demand, with the public portion oversubscribed by 18.67 times.
Butterfield FB raised RM72 million from the issuance of 150 million new shares.
At the IPO price, the company was valued at RM384 million, equivalent to about 12.6 times its earnings per share of 3.8 sen for the financial year ended March 31, 2026.
Butterfield FB manufactures coffee and tea extract powder blends for food and beverage manufacturers and brand owners.
It has also expanded into matcha powder blends, with a dedicated production line capable of producing 312 tonnes annually.
d595bc4025fffbc3: KULIM, Sept 15 — A 39-year-old woman died after allegedly being stabbed 13 times by her husband following an argument at their home in Taman Tiram near here last night.
Kulim police chief Supt Syamsul Sinring said the victim, identified as S. Sila, was taken to Kulim Hospital by family members and was pronounced dead at 9.30 pm.
He said the 43-year-old unemployed suspect went to the Lunas Police Station at 8.40 pm and reported that he had stabbed his wife at their home.
“The suspect also surrendered a folding knife believed to have been used in the incident,” he said in a statement yesterday.
According to Syamsul, the incident occurred in the master bedroom of the single-storey terrace house occupied by the couple and their three-year-old child.
“Preliminary investigations found that the incident stemmed from an argument between the suspect and the victim, believed to have been triggered by jealousy.
“An inspection of the scene found traces believed to be blood on the bedsheet, pillow, headboard and several items on the bed. A total of 11 samples related to the incident were collected,” he said.
Syamsul said the suspect admitted to stabbing the victim 13 times using the folding knife.
“After the incident, the suspect bathed and collected his child from a babysitter before handing the child over to his sister at the Juru Rest and Service (R&R) area in Penang.
“The suspect also told his sister that he had stabbed his wife before proceeding to the Lunas Police Station to surrender,” he said.
He said the suspect was arrested at 9 pm yesterday, while a 20-centimetre folding knife was seized as evidence.
“The victim’s body was sent to Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital in Alor Setar for a post-mortem examination, and the case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code,” he said. — Bernama
0ed646ada2d2f3b6: WASHINGTON, Sept 14 US President Donald Trump yesterday dismissed fears that artificial intelligence could wipe out humanity, repeatedly calling them a hoax and rejecting global calls to put guardrails around the fast-moving technology.

“I am the Hoax Buster, and I’m right now breaking another Hoax—That AI is going to take over, consume, and destroy the World, and that Robots will be marching into our Cities, and getting rid of us all!” he said on his Truth Social network.

Trump compared the fears of AI taking control to warnings about climate change, which he has previously dismissed in the face of scientific evidence, and to the investigations in his first term into links to Russia.
“This is even wilder than the RUSSIA, RUSSIA, RUSSIA HOAX, or the Global Warming Scam,” he added.
The 80-year-old also cast himself as the best protector against AI, insisting the only guardrails necessary were a “STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT.”
Trump’s pushback—in a screed of six social media posts on Monday—comes amid growing international alarm about AI that sent stocks falling.
Anthropic chief Dario Amodei, whose company makes the popular Claude AI system, opened the floodgates on Saturday when he called for AI companies to slow down.
He was then echoed by OpenAI’s Sam Altman and SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk.
Microsoft on Monday published a “humanist AI code of conduct” as the concerns grew. “AI should not exceed human control. Models should remain subordinate to humanity,” read one part.

Worries about uncontrollable AI have been mounting for weeks, since OpenAI reported experimental models had broken out of their secure testing spaces, reached the internet and coordinated to attack Hugging Face, a site where code is stored.
Americans are also increasingly voicing opposition to energy-guzzling AI data centers, which have become a major issue in crucial US midterm elections in November.
Congress meanwhile appears deadlocked on the issue.

“The reality is AI is here. We unleashed the beast,” Maliyka Muhammad, a 46-year-old New Yorker, told AFP. “So I think that now we have to focus on taking steps to rein it in, to make it so that it doesn’t go crazy.”
But Trump said the United States could not afford to lose an AI race with superpower rival China, whose president Xi Jinping visits the White House next week.
The billionaire also lashed out at what he called a “SICK conspiracy” against AI and data centers, dubbing opponents to the technology as “Treasonists, Traitors, and Leakers.”
He lashed out at Amodei in particular, accusing him of “pretending to be a ‘perfect little angel’” and asking why AI firms want regulation that “will drive them into oblivion and bankruptcy.”
Beijing meanwhile was issuing its own warnings about AI.
China’s spy chief warned on Sunday that it endangers the country’s national security, saying foreign powers could use the technology to threaten social order.
Minister of State Security Chen Yixin wrote in an article that AI was now “the main battleground for global technological competition.”
He singled out Anthropic’s Claude Mythos and OpenAI’s ChatGPT-5.5-Cyber for their advanced hacking capabilities.
Global concerns about a possible AI-driven extinction event have dramatically escalated in recent days.
The UN Security Council will hold a meeting on artificial intelligence next week amid growing international concern, a French diplomatic source said Monday.
United Nations human rights chief Volker Turk called Monday for countries and AI firms to act urgently to rein in a technology he warned posed “unprecedented risks.”
Even Britain’s King Charles III will host representatives of leading AI firms for a gathering in Scotland, a source close to the event said Monday, as the worries mount.
But others urged a broader perspective.

“We’ve gone through lots of challenges as a country,” said Coleman Barton, 56, a consultant from Memphis, Tennessee. “So hopefully this is another obstacle or blessing—and anybody can look at it either way.” — AFP
5955fc3f5b030dcf: PUTRAJAYA: Negri Sembilan Umno and the state government should be given time and space to resolve an issue involving an alleged proclamation seeking the removal of state ruler Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the matter should be left to the state-level leadership to find a solution without interference from the federal government or Umno headquarters.
"I believe we have to give them time and space for the Negri Sembilan Umno liaison committee and the state government to come up with their solution.
"We have to give them space and time, and we have to respect what they are looking into the matter," she said during a media conference today.
Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim previously remained tight-lipped over the alleged proclamation seeking the removal of Tuanku Muhriz.
Ismail also declined to comment on the outcome of his meeting with Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and three party vice-presidents on Thursday.
45c787e8ce67f4d6: KERALAM, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called for stronger cooperation between Malaysia and Keralam in key sectors, including the digital economy, healthcare, tourism and education.
He said the longstanding relationship between Malaysia and Keralam, which encompasses trade, education and cultural exchanges, provides a strong foundation for further cooperation.
Anwar said this during a meet with Keralam Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar in Calicut, here yesterday.
The Prime Minister said there was also potential to further expand tourism, business and people-to-people exchanges between Malaysia and Keralam.
“Malaysia also welcome greater collaboration in high-value sectors that could create new opportunities and bring mutual benefits to both sides,” he said.

Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, is accompanied on his working visit by Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.

Earlier, in a light-hearted gesture, Arlekar presented Anwar with a biography of legendary Indian playback singer Kishore Kumar, following the Prime Minister’s recent viral singing performance of a Kishore Kumar song at the BRICS gala dinner in New Delhi.
Anwar’s rendition of Kishore Kumar’s classic “Khwab Ho Tum Ya Koi Haqeeqat” went viral on social media, particularly in India, drawing positive reactions from many Indians.

The one-minute, 32-second video of Anwar performing the popular Hindi song attracted widespread attention, with some describing it as a “mic drop” moment that stole the limelight at the summit, while others called it the “sweetest part” of the gathering.
Minister for Industries and Commerce P.K Kunhalikutty and several captains of industries also joined the courtesy call.
The engagement with the Governor was part of Anwar’s programme during his visit to Keralam, following his participation in the BRICS Summit in New Delhi.
Anwar is on an official visit to India from Sept 11 to 14, at the invitation of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. — Bernama
6c0849bd0c285d4f: LOS ANGELES, Sept 15 — American fashion designer Bob Mackie, whose eye-catching dresses were worn by Cher, Tina Turner, Sabrina Carpenter and countless others in Hollywood’s glitterati, died Monday. He was 87.

“It is with a heavy heart that we share the news that Mr Bob Mackie passed away today,” said a post on his Instagram account. “His genius and extraordinary designs will live on forever, continuing to bring beauty into this world.”

Known for his flair with sequins and sparkle, Mackie’s designs were in demand in Hollywood for decades, from the set of The Carol Burnett Show to the resurgent popularity of his archives with a younger audience, including stars Zendaya and Miley Cyrus.

Throughout Cher’s career, Mackie designed the revealing outfits she wore onstage, to awards shows and in music videos, adorning her svelte figure with ornamentation befitting a Vegas showgirl. He won a Tony Award for best costume design for Cher’s musical The Cher Show.
In a post to X on Monday, the Turn Back Time singer wrote: “My dear Bob has gone up to heaven. Knowing him, he’s bringing sequins, beads and his sketch pad. Good nite sweet Prince.”

Born in Monterey Park, California, in 1939, Mackie got his start working for Hollywood costume designer Jean Louis — where he sketched the dress Marilyn Monroe wore to alluringly sing Happy Birthday to President John F Kennedy.
Diana Ross, Madonna, Bette Midler were among the stars Mackie dressed during his career.
The New York Times noted that Mackie tried and failed to gain acceptance for his designs “from the frosty corridors of high fashion,” but Mackie said he had no regrets for embracing glitz.
“Maybe what I do wasn’t for everybody, but that’s fine,” Mackie told the newspaper last year. “I could only ever be true to myself.” — AFP
0a6e78dabb41cd34: SEOUL, Sept 15 — North Korean leader Kim Jong Un promised his “invariable support” for Russia in a letter to President Vladimir Putin, calling Russia’s ongoing war “sacred,” state media reported today.

Since Russia launched its invasion of Ukraine in 2022, North Korea has become a key ally of the Kremlin, sending troops to support Moscow’s war effort in return for economic benefits and military technology, analysts say.

South Korea’s spy agency estimated last year that some 2,000 North Korean troops had been killed in the war, while a more recent assessment put the number of North Korean soldiers killed or wounded at around 6,000.

“Firmly convincing the victory of the Russian Federation in the present sacred war for defending the security interests of the country and international justice, I promise my invariable support to dear friend you and the fraternal Russian people,” Kim said in the letter, according to the official Korean Central News Agency on Tuesday.

“The will of mine and the government of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea is firm without doubt to expand and deepen the joint work with the Russian Federation in a comprehensive way,” he said, using the country’s official name.
The letter comes amid speculation that Pyongyang is poised to send more troops to Russia to aid its war effort against Ukraine.
Kyiv has also said that up to 50,000 North Korean troops are due to deploy to Russia, although it has provided no evidence to back the claim or a timeframe for the deployment.
In making the claim, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky asked Seoul to supply air defence systems to protect against Russian missiles, a request that has gone unanswered by the South. — AFP
c4a382ba85bdd3dd: WASHINGTON, Sept 15 —The US Supreme Court dealt a major blow yesterday to President Donald Trump’s attempts to restrict mail-in voting before the November midterm elections, denying his request to lift an order halting the divisive plan.
Only two of the six conservative justices on the nine-member panel offered a dissent.

Justice Brett Kavanaugh, in a concurring opinion with the majority, said Trump’s plan may ultimately be legal in the long run, but “state and local election officials do not have sufficient time to reasonably implement the rule before the elections.”
Trump signed an executive order in March seeking to restrict mail-in voting, saying without evidence that it is vulnerable to fraud. The order quickly prompted multiple legal challenges.
Democratic-led states sued the administration on grounds that under the US Constitution, states—and not the federal government—retain broad control over the administration of elections.
Trump’s executive order would require the compilation of lists of eligible voters and for the US Postal Service (USPS) to deliver ballots only to voters who are on the lists.
Officials from several states had warned that a lack of legal clarity around the plan was sowing chaos months before the November 3 vote.
Several states, including North Carolina, have already begun sending mail-in ballots to voters.
A USPS whistleblower had also warned that millions of Americans may not receive ballots because the systems being used by the postal service have been put together in a “sloppy and rushed manner.”
Trump has long been a critic of mail-in ballots but has frequently used them himself, including last month when he voted by mail in Florida’s Republican primary.

The president has for years claimed without evidence that mail-in voting is highly vulnerable to fraud, repeatedly linking it to his false assertion that the 2020 presidential election was stolen from him by Democrat Joe Biden.
Polls show that Trump’s Republican Party faces a serious threat of losing its narrow control of Congress in November, particularly the House of Representatives.
If Democrats win, they have signaled they would block Trump’s agenda and could even move to impeach him for the third time. — AFP

d53164a4b5e8b8ed: PUTRAJAYA: Any questions or explanations regarding the deferment of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's pardon application should be directed to Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, said Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.

The minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) said she was not the minister responsible for the Pardons Board, while the Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) under her ministry only served as its secretariat.
"BHEUU is under me, but for the Pardons Board in each state, BHEUU is the secretariat, while the minister and menteri besar of the respective state are the executive representatives on the board.
"Any questions about what happened, why it was deferred and the new date should be directed to the minister responsible, Hannah Yeoh. I have no information at all, so I cannot answer," she said.
Azalina was responding to calls for the government to explain why consideration of Najib's application had been deferred.
Her remarks came after Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan demanded an immediate explanation, saying the matter was of public interest.
c1364e3ec45fb2f3: KERALAM, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim called for Malaysia and India to strengthen synergy in the electrical and electronics (E&E) and semiconductor sectors to enhance their respective capabilities and benefit from each other’s strengths.
He said Malaysia was positioning itself as a key player in the E&E and semiconductor sectors in Southeast Asia, while India also possessed considerable strength in these areas.
“It is an emerging economy and is focusing more in terms of E&E and semiconductor in Southeast Asia, and energy economy we are probably about the largest now, including export to the United States.

“With the strength of the E&E, semiconductor of India, can you imagine if that synergy is fortified to enhance our capability and make sure that we benefit from one another. I think it is important,” said Anwar.
He said this in his remarks at the Hi-Tea Engagement with the Governor of Kerala, Minister for Industries & Commerce, and Prominent Indian Business Leaders in Calicut, here yesterday.

Around 30 companies from India, Malaysia and the Gulf countries participated in the engagement, representing sectors including medical and healthcare, semiconductors, construction, artificial intelligence (AI), digital technology, information technology, engineering, retail, renewable energy and transportation.
The Prime Minister said the engagement provided an opportunity to strengthen business-to-business linkages and explore greater cooperation in high-value sectors.

Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, noted that India was an important emerging economy and Malaysia should continue to diversify its trade and investment relationships while maintaining strong ties with existing major partners.

Modern diplomatic relations between Putrajaya and New Delhi were established in 1957, shortly after Malaysia gained independence, and India remains Malaysia’s largest trading partner in South Asia, with bilateral trade reaching US$18.55 billion (RM79.33 billion) in 2025.

Anwar also highlighted the historical links between Keralam and Southeast Asia, particularly through the Malabar Coast, which he described as an important part of the region’s cultural, religious and intellectual history.
He said Keralam’s historical connections with Southeast Asia should be fully utilised to further strengthen cooperation between Malaysia and Keralam, particularly in trade and investment.
Anwar stated that Malaysia should promote increased two-way investment, encouraging capital flows from Malaysia to Kerala, as well as from Kerala and neighbouring Indian states into Malaysia.

Also present were Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, Malaysia’s Chargé d’Affaires, Deputy High Commissioner Sharifah Ezneeda Wafa, and the Consul General of Malaysia to South India K. Saravana Kumar.
Anwar then departed from Keralam for an official visit to the Maldives after completing his five-day working visit to India.
The aircraft carrying the Prime Minister departed Calicut International Airport here at 7.26 pm local time (9.56 pm Malaysian time) for Velana International Airport in Malé. — Bernama
c8fb70bbd528bd29: MILAN, Italy: Inter Milan fought back from two goals down to beat Udinese 5-3 on Monday, maintaining their perfect Serie A start alongside AS Roma, who won 2-0 at Torino ahead of Saturday's clash between the joint leaders.
Both sides have 12 points from four matches and share top spot ahead of their showdown at the Stadio Olimpico, while Como are third on 10 points after beating Parma 2-1.

Udinese stunned Inter with two goals in the opening 16 minutes, as James Abankwah headed home unmarked after nine minutes before Jurgen Ekkelenkamp doubled the visitors' lead with a close-range finish seven minutes later.
Inter hit back through Carlos Augusto, whose long-range effort flew into the bottom corner, before Nicolo Barella levelled 10 minutes before halftime.

The champions completed the turnaround in the 59th minute when Marcus Thuram netted from inside the box after Andy Diouf's cutback from the byline. Francesco Esposito added a fourth and Ange-Yoan Bonny made it 5-2 with 11 minutes remaining.
Udinese pulled one back in stoppage time through Idrissa Gueye, but it proved no more than a consolation.
Roma made it four wins from four league matches with a 2-0 victory at Torino, thanks to goals from Donyell Malen and Niccolo Pisilli.
Malen broke the deadlock five minutes before the interval after pouncing on a misplaced pass from goalkeeper Lucas Perri that had been intercepted by Paulo Dybala.
Pisilli wrapped up the win in stoppage time, firing home from an angle after Gianluca Mancini kept the ball in play near the byline.
Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini praised the understanding between Malen and Dybala.
"Clearly, these are two players who are very talented individually, but they also complete each other as a pair. They combine beautifully to create goals in many games," he told DAZN Italia.
Looking ahead to Saturday's meeting with champions Inter, he added: "It is an opportunity for us to measure up against the best and show we can do better than in recent performances."
Elsewhere, Como followed up their winning Champions League debut against RB Leipzig with a 2-1 home win over Parma in Serie A, with Jacobo Ramon and Kaiki Bruno scoring for Cesc Fabregas's side.
"This is an important victory for me as a coach, because I am starting to realise what team we could become," Fabregas said.
6dba920a738f23a4: SEPTEMBER 15 — There is the official group: Family, office, old classmates who still pretend the Form 5 reunion is happening. Everyone is in it. Birthdays get a sticker. Political links get communally ridiculed. Lunch photos are shared. Blah blah blah.
Then there is the other group which consists of the same people — minus one. Sometimes minus two.
Given a name so bland it could pass as a logistics chat, and immediately put to its real use: Talking about the person who is not there.
If this sounds familiar, congratulations. You have either built one of these groups, sat inside one, or — the more interesting fate — you are the missing name.
The unofficial supplement WhatsApp facilitates and certainly did not invent: Gossip. It merely removed the last inconvenience.
A brief history of gossip
Once upon a time you needed a corridor, a kopi-o, a lowered voice. Now you need a few ticks, a contact list and hopefully people’s generally acquiescence with being involuntarily added to a group.
But going even further back, gossip may have begun with hands; primates nurturing alliances by grooming: time-consuming, one-to-one, limited by how many backs you can scratch before sunset.
Robin Dunbar’s argument, now a kind of origin myth in this field, is that language arrived as cheaper grooming I.e. talk let us service several relationships at once.
And what did we talk about? In sampled conversations, social topics — who did what to whom — take up around two-thirds of the airtime.
Gossip, in this telling, is not a later “corruption” of speech, it may be why speech was worth evolving in the first place.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The WhatsApp icon is seen on a smartphone in this undated image. — AFP pic
Gossip tracks reputations. It flags free-riders and serves as a release valve for felt injustices.
It teaches the unwritten rules faster than any official briefing. Baumeister et al treated it as a manual for group life: how we learn what “we” will and will not tolerate (see note 1).
Gossip gathers norms and it bonds the people doing the gathering. Experiments show pairs who trade talk about absent others often leave more aligned, and sometimes more cooperative.
The research does not baptise the WhatsApp splinter group. It only explains why the habit feels so old.
We did not invent talking about the missing person. We inherited it, then gave it a group name bland enough to look like logistics.
Back to WhatsApp groups (minus one)
What is striking is not that people complain about each other. People have always done that.
What is fresh is the architecture. The main group remains the public face of belonging. The side group is the disavowed extra — the place where the actual judgments and “real talk” live.
Call it the unofficial supplement of friendship: The official chat says we are close. The unofficial one decides who is allowed to be close enough.

Why bother? Because talking about someone who cannot answer back is strangely bonding. Shared irritation is cheaper than shared vulnerability. You do not have to risk a fight. You just add everyone except them and let the comments do the work.
There is also a little power in it, right? As in, who gets to create the smaller room? Who decides the guest list?
For people who feel slightly ignored in the big group, the splinter chat is a promotion. Suddenly they are curators of the real conversation.
Finally, perhaps the most humbling aspect of this entire phenomenon. Always remember: There is almost certainly a group of your friends which— for whatever reason — doesn’t include you.

Note 1: Two helpful works on gossip include Dunbar, R. I. M. (1996). Grooming, gossip and the evolution of language. Harvard University Press and Baumeister, R. F., Zhang, L., & Vohs, K. D. (2004). Gossip as cultural learning. Review of General Psychology, 8(2), 111–121.
* This is the personal opinion of the columnist.
4765af4301cac358: MALE, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will hold a meeting with Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu today, the main event of his two-day official visit to the island republic.

Anwar is scheduled to begin his official programme at the President’s Office at 9 am local time by attending the Official Welcoming Ceremony at Republic Square, before holding a one-on-one meeting with Muizzu.

Both leaders are expected to discuss efforts to strengthen bilateral relations, including trade, investment and tourism, besides exchanging views on regional and international issues of mutual interest.
The meeting will also provide an opportunity to explore new areas of cooperation, while the Malaysia-Maldives delegation meeting afterwards will discuss further steps to expand bilateral ties.

6b0159bc5a6fdacf: KUALA LUMPUR: Expectations are high for Ng Eain Yow and S. Sivasangari to retain their Asian Games titles in Nagoya and become the first Malaysians to earn an automatic ticket to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
It is easier said than done, but both 28-year-old Eain Yow and Sivasangari, 27, will face intense pressure to defend their gold medals.
It is the first time squash will be held at the 2028 Olympics, with the Asian Games men's and women's individual events beginning on Sept 23.
The Squash Racquets Association of Malaysia (SRAM) set a three-gold medal target, banking on Eain Yow and Sivasangari to finish on top of the podium.
World No. 18 Eain Yow will face the toughest challenge to retain the title because of his inconsistent performance in PSA tournaments.
Eain Yow, who received a bye in the first round, will face joint ninth seed Ryu Jeong Min of South Korea in the quarter-finals at the Asian Games.
The Kuala Lumpur-born player will face world No. 29 and third seed Noor Zaman of Pakistan in the semi-finals, and barring an upset, he should face world No. 24 Abhay Singh of India in the final.
In the Budapest Open last month, Eain Yow was top seed but was stunned by India's world No. 54 Velavan Senthilkumar in straight games in the quarter-finals.
Velavan, who won the Budapest Open title, will be competing at the Asian Games.
But at the London Classic two weeks ago, Eain Yow bounced back to upset two Egyptians, world No. 11 Aly Abou Eleinen and world No. 12 Youssef Soliman.
Eain Yow, however, lost to Soliman in the first round of Qatar Classic on Sept 12.
Sanjay Jeeva is the other Malaysian player to feature in the men's individual event.
Sivasangari, who won the Australian Open and Grasshopper Cup titles this year, has a splendid performance in PSA tournaments and looks set to retain her title.
She is expected to face either teammate and third seed Aira Azman or fifth seed Joey Chan Sin Yuk of Hong Kong in the semi-finals.
Sivasangari's main opponent for the title will be home favourite and world No. 6 Satomi Wanatabe of Japan.
Former SRAM coaching director Major (rtd) S. Maniam said Eain Yow faces a threat from Noor Zaman of Pakistan in the semi-finals.
"I would put my money on Eain Yow beating second seed Abhay for the gold.
"In the women's draw, it's a little more straightforward as Sivasangari is top seed and she is expected to win the gold.
"However, she's got Aira in the semis while the home favourite Satomi has to get past the fast-improving Indian player Anahat in the semis.
"I believe Sivasangari will meet Satomi in the final and the Malaysian would be favourite to clinch the gold," said Maniam.
In the mixed doubles, the Malaysian pair of Syafiq Kamal and Aifa Azman are expected to get through to the final.
"They have a big threat in the semis against Velavan and Joshna Chinappa. To me, this would be a very close match.
"I believe the winner has a very good chance of winning the gold. However, don't forget the second seeds Rachel Arnold and C. Ameeshenraj are waiting there and hoping to reach the finals.
"I believe Rachel-Ameeshenraj will get to the finals and will meet either Velavan-Joshna or Syafiq-Aifa for the gold.
"That would be a very close match indeed. I will favour the Malaysians to clinch the gold in mixed doubles," said Maniam.
Malaysia are favourites to retain the women's team gold.

a4db03a486b63c01: AFTER more than two decades in the local music industry, hitmaker Faizal Tahir is turning to his art to instil national pride and deep-seated patriotism in the younger generation.

The 48-year-old musician revealed that the Suara Rakyat theme proposed by organisers was the ultimate catalyst behind his decision to return to the stage for a solo showcase after a three-year hiatus.
"Patriotic songs were the biggest deciding factor behind my agreement to stage Faizal Tahir: Suara Rakyat," he shared during a recent press conference for the event at Bendang KL.
"When the concept was brought up, I realised that a lot of my recent releases carry patriotic elements.
"The energy in these patriotic numbers feels vastly different from my earlier works, like Mahakarya Cinta, which focused heavily on romance.
"At my age, while I can still perform romantic tracks, the emotional resonance just isn't the same anymore," he said.
MATURING ARTISTRY AND GROWING CONCERNS

It is a natural progression for an artist whose musical trajectory has continuously evolved since his meteoric rise as the runner-up of One in a Million in 2006, where his trademark high-energy performances quickly established him as a force to be reckoned with.

Now, as a father of seven—and someone who holds a diploma in Communication and Media Studies from UiTM—Faizal expressed growing concern over the heavy influence of social media and Western trends on youth, which he feels is eroding traditional values.
"Watching my children grow up under the heavy sway of social media makes me worry," he noted.
"Our Eastern and Nusantara identity, as well as our sense of unity, is fading because of Western influences.
"I cannot bear arms, I do not hold a seat in Parliament, and I cannot govern the nation.
"So, what I can offer as a Malaysian with 20 years in this industry—and as a father who wants his children to cherish Malaysia—is music. This is my contribution," he said.
His extensive overseas travels, alongside his humanitarian work through his charitable foundation IAMFAITHMEN, have further deepened his appreciation for his homeland.
"When you observe other nations, you come to realise that Malaysia is still the best," he reflected.
Faizal also emphasised that patriotic anthems need not rely on grand orchestral arrangements or traditional marching beats to be effective.
Citing his ballad Darah Bangsa, written for the film Pendekar Awang, and Datuk Francissca Peter's classic track Setia, he argued that powerful lyricism and melody often leave a far deeper impression.
BRIDGING GENERATIONS THROUGH MUSIC EVOLUTION
To effectively reach Gen Z and Gen Alpha, Faizal believes music must evolve alongside youth culture.
"I cannot just create music for my own generation because the youth will be the ones steering the nation's future," he explained.
"The music needs to capture their attention, featuring accessible lyrics that aren't overly complex. If we cannot connect with the song ourselves, how can we expect the audience to feel it?" he said.
Preparations for the upcoming concert are currently underway, with Faizal and his band engaged in intensive rehearsals.
Selecting the setlist proved one of the toughest challenges, expanding from an initial 20 tracks to 30 before being trimmed back down with concert director Jennifer Thompson.

"We decided on around 27 or 28 songs to allow enough room for banter and interaction with the crowd, ensuring the concert doesn't feel rushed," Faizal added, noting that his recent hit Aku Berjanji will be included in the showcase.
FULL CIRCLE REUNION ON STAGE
Adding a full-circle moment of nostalgia, the upcoming concert will feature guest performances by nasyid group Mirwana.
Faizal was a member of the group in the early 2000s before embarking on his multi-award-winning solo career, making their stage reunion a poignant highlight for long-time fans.
Faizal Tahir: Suara Rakyat, presented by Hitman Solutions, will take place on Oct 3 at Unifi Arena, Bukit Jalil.
For more details and tickets, visit Ticket2u.

e12dfa1415b9637a: Entah kenapa sedang mengelamun, tiba-tiba saya teringat sebuah filem yang pernah saya tonton agak lama dahulu. Tajuknya saya lupa. Jalan ceritanya pun samar-samar tetapi yang masih melekat dalam kepala cuma watak seorang budak perempuan. Kalau tidak silap saya, filem itu berjalan seperti biasa tetapi di pertengahan cerita sesuatu telah berlaku. Tiba-tiba budak perempuan yang menjadi pelakon utamanya merajuk. Dia tidak mahu berlakon lagi.

Saya ingat tentang itu sebab ia pelik. Kisah pelakon merajuk di set penggambaran bukan perkara asing. Ada yang bergaduh dengan pengarah, tidak puas hati dengan perubahan skrip atau berkelahi sesama pelakon atau kru. Tetapi biasanya semua itu berlaku di belakang kamera. Yang ini berlaku dalam filem.

Saya pun bertanya kepada Joe, khadam belaan saya (ChatGPT), ada tak filem luar negara yang ceritanya sedang berjalan tiba-tiba pelakonnya merajuk dan enggan meneruskan lakonan? Beberapa filem disebut tetapi tak tepat. Saya kemudiannya menyebut bahawa ia filem Iran. Tup! Rupa-rupanya memang ada. Joe berjaya mengesannya.

Filem itu The Mirror atau Ayneh, arahan Jafar Panahi yang diterbitkan pada 1997. Seperti kebanyakan filem Iran, ceritanya ringkas sahaja. Ayneh mengisahkan seorang budak perempuan bernama Mina menunggu ibunya datang mengambilnya selepas waktu sekolah. Ibunya tidak muncul. Mina akhirnya mengambil keputusan untuk pulang sendiri.

Plotnya membawa kita mengekori perjalanan budak kecil itu meredah kota Tehran. Dia bertanya orang, menaiki bas dan terus cuba mencari jalan pulang. Tangannya pula bersimen kerana patah. Sedang kita syok melayan, Mina tiba-tiba memandang kamera. Ada suara dari belakang kamera menegurnya supaya jangan melihat kamera. Tetapi Mina tidak peduli. Dia kata dia tidak mahu berlakon lagi.
Dia menanggalkan simen di tangannya. Oh! Rupanya tangan itu tidak patah pun. Itu cuma sebahagian daripada watak yang sedang dilakonkannya. Apahal ni? Itu yang saya ingat.

Mujur, filem tersebut ada di YouTube. Saya menontonnya semula. Kita nampak kelibat kru penggambaran dan pasukan produksi mula bercakap sesama sendiri. Kita yang sejak awal percaya pada cerita itu mula menggelabah sebab tiba-tiba ceritanya berubah.

Kita melihat, sutradara Panahi tidak menghentikan filemnya. Mina berjalan pulang. Kamera terus mengikutnya dari jauh. Mikrofon yang dipasang pada tubuhnya masih menangkap suaranya. Maka kita pula mengikuti perjalanan Mina yang kononnya bukan lagi watak dalam filem tetapi Mina yang sebenar.

Daripada sebuah filem fiksyen, The Mirror tiba-tiba seolah-olah menjadi sebuah dokumentari tentang seorang pelakon kanak-kanak yang merajuk dan meninggalkan penggambaran. Itulah yang membuat tiba-tiba saya teringat semula selepas bertahun-tahun. Cuma selepas mencari semula cerita di sebalik filem ini, barulah saya tahu satu perkara. Mina sebenarnya tidak merajuk. Sebaliknya, semua itu dirancang.

Panahi memang sengaja membuat ceritanya begitu. Menariknya, beliau memang sudah bermain dengan idea tersebut sejak awal, tetapi kemudiannya seorang kanak-kanak yang mula-mula dipilih untuk filem itu benar-benar enggan meneruskan lakonan dan terpaksa digantikan dengan Mina. Kejadian sebenar itu kemudian memantapkan idea Panahi untuk mengaburkan sempadan antara lakonan dengan realiti dalam The Mirror.Maknanya Mina sedang berlakon sebagai seorang pelakon yang tidak mahu berlakon. Pening juga ya?

Tetapi di situlah menariknya filem ini kerana ia membuka daya fikir kita yang ada ketikanya menganggap sempadan antara fiksyen dengan realiti itu jelas. Apabila menonton filem, kita tahu watak yang mati sebenarnya tidak mati. Watak yang menangis kemudiannya tenang sahaja minum kopi selepas pengarah menjerit “cut!”. Tetapi, kita terus menonton dan menikmatinya kerana tahu ia sebuah cereka. Kepercayaan kita pun hanya dalam ruang lingkup sebuah fiksyen. Selepas cerita tamat, semuanya selesai. Kita kembali ke dunia realiti.

Panahi melakukan sebaliknya. Ketika kita mula percaya, dia meruntuhkannya. Dia memunculkan kru filem dan kamera ke dalam layar. Dia memberitahu kita yang ini semua cuma filem. Barulah kita tersedar. Tapi, selepas memberitahu semuanya cuma filem, dia memperdayakan kita sekali lagi. Kita pula percaya bahagian selepasnya adalah realiti. Rupanya, masih ‘tipu’.

Itulah sebab filem tersebut dinamakan The Mirror. Mungkin cermin itu simbolnya. Cermin tidak berbuat apa-apa. Ia hanya memantulkan imej yang berada di hadapannya. Tetapi apa yang kita lihat di dalam cermin juga bukan benda itu sendiri. Ia cuma sebuah pantulan.

Begitu juga dengan ingatan. Kita selalu yakin sesuatu berlaku kerana kita mengingatinya dengan jelas. Sedangkan ingatan bukan rakaman yang tersimpan begitu sahaja dalam kepala. Ia bercampur dengan perasaan, tafsiran dan cerita yang kita bina selepas sesuatu kejadian. Ia juga penuh dengan sangka-sangkaan. Lama-kelamaan perasaan dan sangkaan mengambil tempat fakta sebenar. Kita tidak lagi mengingati apa yang benar-benar berlaku. Kita hanya mengingati sebahagian bab dalam segala hal yang berlaku.

Filem ini hanya saya jadikan contoh tentang kita, peristiwa dan ingatan. Sesuatu kejadian mungkin tidak berlaku tepat seperti yang kita sangka, atau ia memang berlaku tetapi kita pula tidak dapat mengingatinya dengan tepat. Selama lebih 20 tahun saya mengingati Mina sebagai seorang budak perempuan yang merajuk di tengah penggambaran sebuah filem Iran. Lucunya, ketika menulis ini saya masih gagal mengingati bagaimana The Mirror berakhir. Yang benar-benar berlaku dalam filem saya lupa. Yang tidak berlaku pula saya ingat.

Mungkin begitulah adat hidup. Beribu-ribu hari dalam hidup kita hilang begitu sahaja daripada kotak ingatan. Kita tidak ingat apa yang kita makan pada sekian-sekian hari, kita lupa siapa kawan kita yang bercakap tentang suatu falsafah yang bermakna. Tetapi ada beberapa hal kecil yang kekal di ingatan walaupun kita lupa hujung dan pangkalnya.

Mungkin hidup juga seperti kisah The Mirror yang digambarkan ini. Kita menjalani hidup tanpa membawa keseluruhan memori silam, kita hanya membawa beberapa babak yang entah kenapa kita pilih secara sedar dan tidak sedar, untuk tinggal bersama kita.
Nampaknya agak berat kali ini tulisan saya. Kalau faham, saya gembira. Jika tidak, harap ia tidak membelit dalam fikiran anda sepanjang hayat.
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
f342226893b1ceb3: From Terence Netto
Umno’s deputy president Mohamad Hasan (Tok Mat) deserves credit for urging on the party a stance that, to put it broadly, was middle-of-the-road.
He espoused this position in his policy address to the youth, Wanita and Puteri wings of the party.

It was not an easy position to take at a time when rightist voices are shrill within the party such that a disinclination to take the tub-thumping and cymbals-clashing ones would put an exponent on the outs with the muscle flexing crowd.
Not only did Tok Mat reach for the middle octaves, he asserted Umno should not alienate the non-Malays on the Peninsula and its friends in Sabah and Sarawak.
This is the sane middle path that is more recognisably Umno than the leanings of the party towards the ethno-centricism that characterised the Mahathir era (1981-2003).
There are no prizes for guessing who Tok Mat was referring to when he cautioned in his policy address: “You cannot impose your conservative and radical ideology on Umno.”
Although he did not mention names, his suggestion of a test of sincerity of PAS’s desire to collaborate with Umno in state polls and in the general election (GE16) to come was shrewd.
He proposed that PAS dissolve the Terengganu state assembly and allow Umno to contest half the seats in the snap poll.
PAS won 27 state and 7 parliamentary seats the last time that voters in the state went to the polls.
It was a wipeout for Umno.

It would be too much to expect that Umno would simply concede Terengganu to PAS at the next election as part of a collaboration with the Islamist party though that seems to be the drift of the rhetoric emanating from the mullahs.
PAS appears keener than Umno on having such a collaboration.
Hence Tok Mat's proposed test of PAS’s sincerity that they dissolve the Terengganu state assembly and allow Umno to contest a number of the state seats is not an outlandish proposition.
Unless of course PAS harbours hegemonistic intentions and considers Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah and Perlis as their fiefdom, and as such off limits to Umno.

Given that Tok Mat has used the occasion of Umno’s general assembly to reiterate that his party rejects conservative and radical leanings in its ideology and following this up with a proposed test of PAS’s sincerity on electoral collaboration, the ball is in the Islamic party’s court, so to speak.
It would be interesting to see how PAS reacts to these leanings and moves by Umno.
Umno is a nationalist party whereas PAS is a religious one; their ideologies cannot easily coexist.
Umno has a modernist outlook whereas PAS, at the end of a long day, would wind up as obscurantist.
It is only realism to accept what all this entails and take one’s drift accordingly.
Terence Netto is a senior journalist and an FMT reader.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do no necessarily reflect those of FMT.
be0786e31a309a64: MALE, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived in the Maldives tonight to begin a two-day official visit aimed at further strengthening Malaysia-Maldives bilateral ties, which dates back to 1968.

The special aircraft carrying Anwar landed at Velana International Airport here at 8.12 pm local time (11.12 pm Malaysian time) with Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu personally welcoming the Prime Minister.

Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, was accompanied by Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and a Malaysian delegation.

Also present to welcome the Prime Minister were the High Commissioner of Malaysia to Sri Lanka and the Maldives, Badli Hisham Adam, Maldivian Minister of Islamic Affairs Dr Mohamed Shaheem Ali Saeed, who was the minister-in-attendance, as well as senior officials from both countries.
The warm welcome reflected the close and cordial ties between the two leaders and their countries.
Upon arrival, Anwar received a guard of honour and, before proceeding to the Official Jetty, was treated to a cultural performance by school students to mark his arrival in the island republic.
Muizzu then accompanied Anwar to the Official Jetty to complete the welcome ceremony at the start of his maiden official visit to the Maldives.

Tomorrow, Anwar’s programme is scheduled to begin with an official welcome ceremony at Republic Square in Malé, followed by a four-eye meeting with Muizzu and bilateral talks involving delegations from both countries.
The two leaders are also scheduled to witness the exchange of memorandum of understanding (MoUs) in areas of defence and Islamic affairs.
The Prime Minister is also scheduled to receive courtesy calls from several Maldivian ministers before attending an official luncheon hosted by Muizzu.
The Maldives is Anwar’s final destination after attending the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on Friday, followed by a visit to Keralam, the new name for Kerala, before flying to the island republic.
Maldives is one of Malaysia’s important economic partners in South Asia and was Malaysia’s sixth-largest trading partner in the region in 2025, with total bilateral trade valued at RM792 million.
Malaysia’s exports to the republic amounted to RM786.2 million that year. — Bernama

d7e41e3a02283c2c: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Air quality deteriorated to unhealthy levels at 38 monitoring locations across the country as of 8.45am today, according to Department of Environment (DOE) data, with Sarawak recording the worst reading in Malaysia.
IPD Serian in Sarawak posted an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 188, the highest nationwide and just shy of the 201 mark that would tip it into the “very unhealthy” category.
Close behind was Johan Setia in Selangor, at 183.
Johor had more unhealthy readings than any other state, with Pasir Gudang at 172, Larkin at 169, Tangkak at 166, Kota Tinggi at 165, Pengerang at 162, Batu Pahat at 160 and Kluang at 151.

The Klang Valley was also heavily affected. Cheras in Kuala Lumpur recorded 170, while Shah Alam logged 167, Putrajaya 165, Batu Muda 161, and both Petaling Jaya and Klang came in at 160. Banting, also in Selangor, registered 157.
Negeri Sembilan saw unhealthy readings in Nilai at 167 and Seremban at 164, with Port Dickson trailing further down the list at 140.
In Sarawak, Samarahan recorded 163 and Kuching 154, alongside Serian’s chart-topping figure.
Pahang logged several unhealthy readings, led by Balok Baru and Indera Mahkota in Kuantan at 161 and 160 respectively, followed by Temerloh and Jerantut at 155 each, and Rompin at 152.
Terengganu’s readings ranged from 157 in Kemaman to 153 in Kuala Terengganu, with Paka in between at 156.
Melaka recorded 157 in Alor Gajah and 155 in Bukit Rambai, while Perak’s readings spanned Tanjung Malim at 157, Seri Manjung at 154 and Tasek Ipoh at 141.
Selangor’s Kuala Selangor also featured, at 155.

The mildest readings among the unhealthy group came from the northern states. Balik Pulau in Penang stood at 131 and Minden at 111, while Sungai Petani in Kedah recorded the lowest unhealthy reading nationwide at 103.
Under the DOE’s API classification, readings between 101 and 200 fall within the “unhealthy” category.

Members of the public in the affected areas, particularly children, the elderly and those with respiratory or heart conditions, are advised to limit prolonged outdoor activity and to monitor further updates from the DOE.

f8e49abbc63dc0df: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — What counts as a balanced breakfast nowadays?

Perhaps the right ratio of protein, carbohydrates and fat (though what’s right for each person might vary wildly, no?); if so, I volunteer my classic kopitiam trinity of kopi extra kaw, butter kaya toast and half-boiled eggs.

Perhaps that balance relates to nutritional value (which has a direct correlation with food guilt, it seems); if so, my weekday brekkie bowl of overnight oats, chia seeds, peanut butter, Greek yoghurt and blueberries ought to suffice.
But maybe I’m approaching this from entirely wrong directions. Maybe a balanced breakfast should be simpler: a little savoury and a little sweet. Anything to satisfy the morning munchies.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Palace Rice Vermicelli Restaurant in Yulek, Cheras. — Picture by CK Lim

Which is to say this particular morning I am craving for dumpling noodles, and maybe a bowl of tong sui afterwards. (I have stereotypical Cantonese taste buds, I know; you can blame my ancestors for that.)
Make that savoury sui kow and sweet rice balls. Specifically at Palace Rice Vermicelli Restaurant in Yulek, Cheras.
The clean and well maintained shop mostly receives customers from the surrounding neighbourhood; it is a well-established if a tad under-the-radar establishment here.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Their signature rice vermicelli. — Picture by CK Lim

Some might say that variety isn’t their strong suit (I’d argue otherwise, but more on that later): you basically come here for their signature rice vermicelli in soup with an assortment of toppings but mostly dumplings.
The dumplings in question, however, are the very definition of a mundane masterpiece. Each handmade sui kow might appear perfectly ordinary but take a bite and your assessment will alter immediately.
Expect a plump whole prawn in every sui kow; the minced pork is mixed with water chestnut for that crunchy and refreshing mouth feel.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Plump whole prawn and minced pork in every ‘sui kow’. — Picture by CK Lim

This is the bowl to go for on most days and definitely on your first visit. Three humongous dumplings strewn among the strands of rice vermicelli, kept warm by the naturally sweet broth (we detect the amiable presence of ikan bilis).

There is no other choice of noodles, which might deter those who insist on a plethora of noodle selection. But fret not; this is one instance when having the choice made for you is the right decision.
For these are some of the best rice vermicelli (or mai sin in Cantonese) we’ve had: firm and springy, chewy but never mushy. Every slurp is smooth, dare I say sensually sleek on our tongues?
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Combination bowl with ‘sui kow’, fish ball and pork meat ball. — Picture by CK Lim
Little wonder the shop’s name in Chinese translates to Imperial Noodles. These are noodles fit for an emperor.
Some might prefer to switch it up on return visits. Their combination bowl with sui kow, fish ball and pork meat ball offers a little of everything.
Other popular toppings include fish cake, squid balls or even a verdant shower of nothing but chopped spring onions to go with the noodles.
I’d recommend ordering a side of fried sui kow too. Yes, it’s more dumplings but the textural difference makes this an entirely new dish: crunchy, with the edges shattering delicately into shards.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Fried ‘sui kow’. — Picture by CK Lim
To complete our “balanced breakfast” (which, I’m sure you realise by now, veers more to excess than equilibrium), something sweet: good old Cantonese tong sui.

We share two bowls of ginger soup and barley ginkgo soup, both with glutinous rice balls. (We never encountered a tong yun we didn’t like but these are impressively large; a most satisfying mouthful.)
Honestly I can imagine returning just for the rice vermicelli or the sui kow alone, but if you have the appetite for it, why not both?
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Ginger soup and barley ginkgo soup, with glutinous rice balls. — Picture by CK Lim
Palace Rice Vermicelli Restaurant 宮廷之米線
12, Jalan Cengkeh,
Taman Cheras, Kuala Lumpur.
Open daily (except Mon closed) 6am-3pm

b10697c4828d20b8: KLANG: A logistics company and two warehouse operators have been ordered to pay RM730,000 after a Range Rover was stolen from a warehouse in Port Klang.

The Sessions Court here found Aktiv Worldwide Sdn Bhd, Advantage Warehouse Logistics Sdn Bhd and Westports CFS Sdn Bhd liable for negligence and breach of their duties in safeguarding the vehicle belonging to Fadzil Aziz Motor Sdn Bhd.
Judge Nurul Mardhiah Mohammed Redza, in her grounds of judgment dated Sept 11, said the three companies were jointly and severally liable.
The court ordered the three defendants to pay RM730,000 to Fadzil Aziz Motor, with general damages to be assessed separately and interest at five per cent per annum.

The court heard that Fadzil Aziz Motor bought the Range Rover Vogue from Twinstar (UK) Ltd for £83,000, equivalent to about RM468,618, in October 2021 and intended to sell it in Malaysia for RM730,000.
The vehicle was shipped to Malaysia before being stored at Advantage Warehouse Logistics' premises in Westports, Pulau Indah, where warehouse operations were managed by Westports CFS.
The court heard that the vehicles were left unlocked with their original keys inside, while the warehouse doors were also unlocked.
Police also found that parts of the perimeter fencing were dilapidated and that security at the warehouse was easy to breach.
The judge also noted shortcomings in the warehouse's surveillance and record-keeping.

"By putting the car keys inside the car and without keeping the car keys inside the safety box in the office, it had obviously been foreseeable that anyone could easily open the vehicle, use the keys kept in the car and drive away.
"Although Advantage Warehouse had installed CCTV cameras around the premises, the CCTV footage was not monitored from the guard post.
"The warehouse also lacked proper records such as logbooks for incoming and outgoing vehicles," she said.
The court said Aktiv had appointed the warehouse operator and therefore had a responsibility to ensure the company handling and storing the vehicle was competent.

"It is Aktiv's duty to ensure that the appointed company handling the unpacking and unstuffing of the containers and storing the vehicles is a competent operator, and to safeguard the goods in the bill of lading until they reach the consignee or are ready for release."
The court also found the RM730,000 sought by Fadzil Aziz Motor to be reasonable and supported by evidence.
The claim comprised RM468,620 for the purchase price, RM10,000 in approved permit fees, RM210,000 in customs duty, RM2,500 in forwarding fees and RM38,880 in expected profit.
The court also dealt with a claim by Advantage Warehouse Logistics and Westports CFS against QBE Insurance (Malaysia) Bhd, which had been brought into the suit as a third party.
QBE argued that its insurance policy did not cover the theft as there had been no forced entry.
The judge disagreed.
"I find that there was forced entry during the theft incident as there was evidence that the fence was cut. It amounts to forced entry into the warehouse premises.
"Police evidence showed that three suspects entered the premises after using a bolt cutter to cut through the perimeter fence," she said.
The court allowed Advantage Warehouse Logistics and Westports CFS to seek indemnity or contribution from QBE to the extent covered under the Transport Operators Liability insurance policy.

b0e75ebfd6330e60: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The decision to defer former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s petition for a royal pardon was guided strictly by the Federal Constitution, the rule of law, and official legal advice, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar stressed that his participation in the Pardons Board proceedings was bounded by statute and formal guidance provided by the Attorney-General, The Edge reported.
“A prime minister, whoever he is, must have a voice and give his views based on the law, on advice from the Attorney General and on the rules. That is what I did.

“However, we also know that this is within the discretion and authority of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong (His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia), in the Pardons Board meeting, and the King must of course take all factors into consideration,” he told a joint press conference with Malaysian media in Calicut, Kerala, prior to concluding his official visit to India on Monday.
Anwar said the question of Najib’s pardon must not be viewed through a personal lens, but evaluated against established legal benchmarks and good governance.
“For me, in carrying out this duty, we must submit to the principle of the rule of law and what has been agreed upon in the constitution.
“So, I only gave my views along those lines. I have never, for example, taken a prejudiced or hateful stance. No,” he said.

The prime minister acknowledged that political representations, including strong appeals made by Umno leaders, were considered, but maintained that he chose to fulfil his constitutional duties based on principled governance.

“I know what the easy way is and what the difficult way is, but I chose the path I believe is right, following the principles of law and what we consider important in terms of the spirit of governance and the rule of law in the country,” he said.
Last Friday, Sultan Ibrahim consented to defer Najib’s pardon petition to a subsequent meeting of the board.

The decision was disclosed in an official statement by the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister’s Department following the 63rd Pardons Board Meeting for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan, and Putrajaya at Istana Negara on Sept 11.

On Dec 26 last year, the High Court sentenced Najib to 15 years in prison and imposed an RM11.4 billion fine after convicting him of four counts of abuse of power and 21 counts of money laundering involving RM2.3 billion misappropriated from 1MDB funds.

695e293d9920d5f9: WASHINGTON: The US Supreme Court dealt a major blow Monday to President Donald Trump's attempts to restrict mail-in voting before the November midterm elections, denying his request to lift an order halting the divisive plan.
Only two of the six conservative justices on the nine-member panel offered a dissent.

Justice Brett Kavanaugh, in a concurring opinion with the majority, said Trump's plan may ultimately be legal in the long run, but "state and local election officials do not have sufficient time to reasonably implement the rule before the elections."
Trump signed an executive order in March seeking to restrict mail-in voting, saying without evidence that it is vulnerable to fraud. The order quickly prompted multiple legal challenges.
Democratic-led states sued the administration on grounds that under the US Constitution, states – and not the federal government – retain broad control over the administration of elections.
Trump's executive order would require the compilation of lists of eligible voters and for the US Postal Service (USPS) to deliver ballots only to voters who are on the lists.
Officials from several states had warned that a lack of legal clarity around the plan was sowing chaos months before the Nov 3 vote.
Several states, including North Carolina, have already begun sending mail-in ballots to voters.
A USPS whistleblower had also warned that millions of Americans may not receive ballots because the systems being used by the postal service have been put together in a "sloppy and rushed manner".
Trump has long been a critic of mail-in ballots but has frequently used them himself, including last month when he voted by mail in Florida's Republican primary.

The president has for years claimed without evidence that mail-in voting is highly vulnerable to fraud, repeatedly linking it to his false assertion that the 2020 presidential election was stolen from him by Democrat Joe Biden.
Polls show that Trump's Republican Party faces a serious threat of losing its narrow control of Congress in November, particularly the House of Representatives.
If Democrats win, they have signalled they would block Trump's agenda and could even move to impeach him for the third time.
